newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SICOM says no plan to dissolve coffee contract.
newsitem.headline: SICOM says no plan to dissolve coffee contract.

text.p: The general manager of the Singapore Commodity Exchange (SICOM) said on Thursday it has no plans to abandon its almost moribund robusta coffee contract.
"The current robusta contract is still around," Lim Toh Eng, SICOM general manager, told Reuters. "We have no plan to dissolve the contract."

The robusta contract, the world's third after London and New York, was launched last year and was aimed at providing hedging facilities for growers and roasters, particularly in Indonesia, during the Asian day between New York's close and London's opening.
But it has failed to take off and little, if any trade, is conducted in the contract, traders said. Roasters and speculators have made very little use of the market.
"The market has not been doing very well," Lim said, adding however that the coffee market has been in the doldrums.
He said the contract is being monitored by SICOM.
Indonesian industry officials have recently said privately that they had given up hope on SICOM.
"I think Indonesia is still interested," Lim said.
